description: Forschungszentrum Jülich publishes EnergyEmissionsRegio, a Python workflow for distributing national final energy use and emissions to local administrative units. The README describes sector-specific spatial proxies, missing-value imputation and disaggregation functions. Public source is free under MIT. The workflow can generate municipal demand and emissions inputs for local energy or climate simulations, with model-pypsa-eur representing a related planning context. A caveat is that a proxy-based allocation is an estimate, not direct consumption or stack measurement at each locality. Country data definitions, administrative boundaries and proxy years need reconciliation before transferring the code beyond the documented Germany and Spain example. The repository metadata and README were read, but dependencies were not installed, the pipeline was not run, and agreement with the published Zenodo tables was not tested. The output data are assessed separately.
